# Pricing Check-In 2026-06-18

My seven-month check on the "no day rates" rule, held at the June Solo Studio Circle session. Result: a partial reversal. A $720 day rate is back for audits, workshops and engagements under 10 days. Value-based three-option proposals stay for anything over 10 days.

## At a Glance

> [!info]
> Rule from 2026-06-18: audits, workshops and work under 10 days are quoted at $720 a day with a fixed number of days. Projects over 10 days get three value-based options with a paid first step. Tallowmere was the first quote under this rule.

## Why I held it

Two things in spring 2026 did not fit the November decision ([[pricing-decision-2025-11-20]]):

1. Two small audit leads, in March and April, went quiet after I sent them three options. One told me afterwards that her board compares suppliers on day rates and my proposal "didn't have one".
2. [[velora-pitch]]. I broke my own rule and sent one price of $74,000; Velora chose Orchard & Vane's $38,000 discovery phase ([[velora-feedback-call-2026-06-03]]). The lesson there was about options and a smaller first step, not about day rates, but it made me look again at the whole model.

## What happened

I brought the [[effective-day-rate-sheet]] updated to May 2026 and the [[circle-rate-survey-2026-06]], which five of the other six members filled in anonymously.

[[rosalind-ng]] made the case she had made in November, with numbers this time. Audit and workshop buyers are usually a manager with a supplier list and a budget line. They compare day rates because that is what their procurement form asks for. For a scope under two weeks, the value-based work of discovery and options costs me a day that I can't bill. Her content audits at a day rate had a higher win rate than my options proposals for similar work.

The survey supported her: the four members who quote day rates for short work charge between $640 and $800; the median is $700.

[[imani-clarke]] added that day rates help partner work: she can price her part of a proposal in days and I can wrap it in options.

[[nadia-ferro]] argued the other way: day rates cap what I can earn on a fast job. True, but for audits I can't see much value-based upside anyway; the client's value is a fix list, not revenue.

## Decision

- $720 a day for audits, workshops and engagements under 10 days, quoted as a fixed number of days with the deliverable named. Up from $650 in 2025, roughly in line with the survey median plus my accessibility specialism.
- Three value-based options with a paid first step for projects over 10 days, unchanged ([[three-option-proposals]], [[paid-discovery-phase]]).
- The rate goes on request only, not on the site ([[should-i-publish-rates-on-my-site]]).
- Written up as [[pricing-rules-2026]] and [[services-menu-2026]]; the proposal template got a short day-rate variant ([[proposal-template-2026]]).

## What happened next

- Tallowmere asked for a day-rate quote because its board compares day rates. 8 days at $720, $5,760 ([[tallowmere-audit-quote-2026-09]], [[tallowmere-ticketing-audit]]). Exactly Rosalind's case.
- Rate review set for January 2027 ([[when-should-the-day-rate-rise]]).
- My stance is now in [[day-rates-suit-small-fixed-work]].
